about: Lesson A13 (a13-fairness-jobs), 2026-11-06, builder learn-w5-b. Part 1 splits the yearly cost of a Prairie City plan across its five household groups (prairie-city.json, read and never retyped) by kWh, by a fixed charge and in proportion to income, and reads energy burden before and after; the cost is a learner input. Part 2 counts jobs and Ridge County's tax base when its coal plant retires and wind and solar are built there; every coefficient (jobs per $M, jobs per 100 MW, the multiplier, displacement, the tax rate, the taxable share) is a learner input set for teaching, with the sources real coefficients come from. Every output is a screening estimate. The accounting is the pure model assets/learn/a13-who-pays-and-benefits.js (LX.A13), which SB3 and C3 can load.

plan.what: the yearly cost of a Prairie City plan that its households pay through their electricity bills (illustrative; an annual amount in 2025 dollars, such as the yearly charge that recovers new wires and programmes)

designs.name: Per kWh
designs.note: households pay in proportion to the electricity they use

designs.name: Fixed charge
designs.long: the same yearly charge for every household
designs.note: every household pays the same dollars

designs.name: By income
designs.long: a charge in proportion to household income
designs.note: every household pays the same share of its income; real income-based designs use a few income tiers

two.name: Two groups
labels: 80% of area median income or more

ridgeCounty.note: Ridge County is Prairieland's coal-dependent county (curriculum v2 §6, scale S4). A13 sets its numbers here and wave W6 (SB4, C4) reuses them: change them together with W6. Anchors from the national-strategy dossier §8.0: Prairieland has 20 million people; Ridge County holds 3% of its workforce; coal provides 40% of the county's local tax revenue. Everything else is set for teaching.
ridgeCounty.fiction: Ridge County and Prairieland are fictional; their numbers are illustrative.
ridgeCounty.set: teaching: the workforce, the county's tax revenue other than the plant's ($840M a year, of which $300M is paid by the coal mines), the plant's size, staff, taxable value and the mine jobs that supply it

jobs.set: teaching: every coefficient is a learner input with an illustrative default, not a prediction; the local share of construction spending (30%), the two building years and the 20-year horizon are fixed for the lesson

tax.set: teaching: one effective property tax rate for the plant and the new farms; the new farms' taxable value as a share of their cost (abatements and depreciation lower it)

jediResults.title: Interpreting JEDI Results
